channel.title: Bills News Consolidated
channel.description: Buffalo Bills news with personalities — daily articles on news, film, culture, comedy and The Card, plus The BNC Blitz newsletter.

item.title: Bills trade for Titans safety Amani Hooker, the NFL's interception leader
item.description: Buffalo traded a 2027 second-round pick to Tennessee for safety Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-rounder, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. Hooker's five interceptions are tied for the NFL lead — three came against Joe Burrow on Nov. 1 — and he fills the hole left by C.J. Gardner-Johnson's release.

item.title: Buffalo's defense just did something no team has done since the 1985 Bears
item.description: Buffalo's 23-6 win at Minnesota came with a historic defensive line, per the Democrat and Chronicle: a second straight game with 3+ turnovers, multiple sacks, under 200 yards allowed, a sub-50% opposing QB and no passing TD — a five-part feat last matched in consecutive games by the 1985 Bears. Minnesota went 0-for-10 on third and fourth down.

item.title: Nine yards for Allen, 34 for Cook: both Bills can pass 5,000 rushing yards tonight
item.description: Per the Bills' PR team, Josh Allen enters Monday night with 4,991 career rushing yards and James Cook with 4,966 — nine and thirty-four yards from both passing 5,000 on the same night, in Minnesota, where Cook's brother Dalvin starred and Adrian Peterson enters the Ring of Honor at halftime.

item.title: Dion Dawkins didn't practice all week. Buffalo still won't rule him out for Monday night.
item.description: Buffalo's final injury report is in: Dion Dawkins (rib) missed all three practices and is questionable for Monday night at Minnesota, Alec Anderson (ankle) upgraded to limited Saturday and is also questionable, and Joshua Palmer is out — while Spencer Brown, DJ Moore, Dalton Kincaid and Keon Coleman were all cleared with no designation.

item.title: The Card: Buffalo is favored in Minnesota, but Friday's injury report is moving the real price
item.description: [Partner Content — paid promotion] Buffalo is a 3.5-point road favorite at Minnesota for Monday night, per the AP preview. Then Friday's practice report landed: Dion Dawkins missed a second straight day (rib), Alec Anderson stayed out (ankle), Spencer Brown stayed limited (back) — and the Vikings got two starters back to full. The Card prices what changed.

item.title: Carson Wentz will start Monday night. Buffalo's bigger problem is its own offensive line.
item.description: Minnesota ruled Kyler Murray out Thursday and named Carson Wentz the starter for Monday night. Buffalo's first practice report was the scarier document: Dion Dawkins (rib) and Alec Anderson (ankle) did not practice and Spencer Brown (back) was limited — both tackles and a guard, three days before Brian Flores' No. 1 defense.

item.title: Justin Jefferson torched Buffalo for 193 yards in 2022. Monday, he gets his rematch.
item.description: Buffalo has faced Justin Jefferson exactly once — in November 2022, when he caught 10 for 193 yards and made the fourth-and-18 catch Bills fans still see in their sleep, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Monday night he gets his rematch: frustrated, underused at 28 catches for 335 yards, and lined up against Christian Benford.

item.title: No. 1 offense meets No. 1 defense Monday night. History says neither survives intact.
item.description: Buffalo at Minnesota on Monday night is just the seventh time since 2017 that the No. 1 offense in EPA per play meets the No. 1 defense, per Buffalo Rumblings. History's verdict: a 3-3 split, the top offense's EPA collapsing from +0.217 to +0.059 — and somebody's ranking exposed.

item.title: Buffalo Bills release C.J. Gardner-Johnson one day after his suspension ended
item.description: One day after C.J. Gardner-Johnson's one-game suspension ended, the Bills released their starting safety instead of bringing him back. The reported reason wasn't the spitting incident — it was the tape.

item.title: From the booth, Leonhard blitzed all afternoon. Was that Buffalo's new defense?
item.description: Buffalo set season highs in man coverage (54.8%), blitz rate (61.3%) and closed-middle looks (67.7%) against Baltimore, per Buffalo Rumblings — with Jim Leonhard calling plays from the booth for the first time. Brady confirmed the booth stays. Monday night in Minnesota decides whether the rest was real.

item.title: Josh Allen passed Jim Kelly with Kelly in the building. This record wasn't about numbers.
item.description: With 12:18 left Sunday, Josh Allen's 11-yard touchdown to DJ Moore was his 259th career passing touchdown — one more than Jim Kelly, who was in attendance at Highmark Stadium. Buffalo beat Baltimore 36-10 to move to 6-1, and the franchise record book changed hands in front of the man who wrote it.

item.title: Buffalo signed three defensive backs on Halloween. That tells you today's real story.
item.description: Buffalo signed Te'Cory Couch and elevated Geno Stone and A.J. Woods on Saturday — a Halloween roster shuffle that says more about today's Ravens game than any prediction. With C.J. Gardner-Johnson suspended and Dee Alford trending out, the Bills rebuilt their secondary depth the night before Lamar Jackson returns.

item.title: Pick your poison: Buffalo can't let Henry and Flowers both eat
item.description: Lamar Jackson is back with no designation, and with him comes Buffalo's hardest choice of the season: load up on Derrick Henry and give Zay Flowers space, or protect Flowers and let Henry dictate. Here's why Buffalo can survive one — but not both.

item.title: Ed Oliver went full. Spencer Brown and Dee Alford went the other way.
item.description: Ed Oliver went from limited Wednesday to a full participant Thursday — the best news of Ravens week. But Spencer Brown missed a second straight practice and Dee Alford was downgraded to out, and Friday's final designations now decide Buffalo's edges.

item.title: He played through a torn ACL. Now Tyrell Shavers is back.
item.description: Tyrell Shavers tore his ACL in last season's Wild Card game — and stayed in it. Designated to return and back at practice Wednesday, he drew the quote of the week from Josh Allen: 'one of the best teammates I've ever had.'

item.title: Bills Mafia's trade deadline wishlist, ranked by delusion
item.description: The deadline is Nov. 10, the cap room is $4.1 million, and Bills Mafia's wishlist ranges from a genuinely sensible safety to a defensive tackle who already plays for the 49ers. We rank all five names by delusion.

item.title: 3 Reasons Derrick Henry Can't Hurt the Buffalo Bills
item.description: The history is scary — 102 yards a game and 11 touchdowns against Buffalo. The current form is not. Henry is limping into Sunday at 3.02 yards a carry over his last two, and the reasons go deeper than one slump.

item.title: The King Has Hit the Cliff: Derrick Henry by the Numbers
item.description: For a decade, Derrick Henry averaged 102 yards a game against Buffalo. The last two weeks: 103 yards total, at 3.02 a carry. We break down the cliff — and the one big reason to be careful before burying the King.

item.title: The Card: 3 trades I like for Ravens at Bills, and the matchup numbers behind them
item.description: [Partner Content — paid promotion] New desk, same rule: only numbers that are real. Matt Manzella opens The Card with the PFF matchup grades behind Ravens at Bills — Cook's 5.34 a carry, Benford's 124.4 problem, Baltimore's 48-0 collapse across its last two second halves — and the three trades he's making on Kalshi.

item.title: Buffalo Bills Just Got GREAT News About Lamar Jackson
item.description: Lamar Jackson is expected back for Nov. 1 — but "expected" is doing a lot of work in that sentence. What a week of conflicting reports actually tells us about Sunday at Highmark Stadium.

item.title: The James Cook number nobody is talking about: 5.34 yards a carry
item.description: Josh Allen gets the headlines, but Buffalo's offense runs on schedule because of one number: James Cook is averaging 5.34 yards per carry. These are the plays that make it real.

item.title: BNC Daily Links: the bye week is over, Ravens week is here
item.description: Your Monday morning roundup: Lamar watch begins, the trade deadline series launches, a Cook stat worth your coffee, and everything else Bills fans need to start Ravens week.

item.title: Why Buffalo's defense gives up yards but not Sundays
item.description: 31st in yards, 5–1 in the standings. We break down the bend-don't-break math behind Jim Leonhard's defense — and the one drive per game where it almost breaks.

item.title: DJ Moore picked Buffalo. Buffalo should return the favor.
item.description: A new receiver, a new city, and a fan base that adopts its players like family. What the DJ Moore era has to get right off the field before it works on it.

item.title: Trade deadline board: 5 names, one per day, starting with the secondary
item.description: The Nov. 10 deadline is coming and Buffalo's cap room is not. A week-long series on who fits, who doesn't, and who is a fantasy — starting where the need is obvious.

item.title: Keon Coleman's stat line is lying to you (in a good way)
item.description: 19 catches, zero drops, a 138.0 passer rating when targeted. Keon Coleman's breakout is quieter than the highlights — and more real. Here's why the boring numbers are the story.

item.title: Power Rankings of AFC Teams I Am Choosing to Disrespect This Week
item.description: The Chiefs are somehow both washed and inevitable. The Jets are a group project nobody did. This week's official disrespect rankings, compiled responsibly during the bye week.

item.title: Game day starts here: your Ravens-week ticket guide
item.description: [Partner Content — paid promotion] Where to sit, when to buy, and what the new-stadium market is doing to prices for Ravens at Bills on Sunday, Nov. 1 — your complete game-week ticket game plan.
